question: Which of the following best describes the Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY)?

answers.text: A free drug and diagnostic entitlement scheme for pregnant women and newborns at public facilities

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This describes Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK), not JSY. JSY is a cash transfer scheme.

answers.text: A conditional cash transfer scheme to promote institutional delivery, with higher incentives for BPL women in low-performing states

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. JSY (2005) provides conditional cash transfers to BPL women who deliver in government facilities. Incentive amounts are higher in Low Performing States (LPS): ₹1,400 rural, ₹1,000 urban.

answers.text: A government insurance scheme covering delivery costs at empanelled private hospitals

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Government insurance for delivery costs (including private hospitals) is covered under PMJAY (Ayushman Bharat), not JSY.

answers.text: A programme providing iron-folic acid supplementation throughout pregnancy

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: IFA supplementation during pregnancy is part of ANC under PMSMA and routine NHM services, not a specific function of JSY.

overallFeedback.feedback: JSY (Janani Suraksha Yojana) is a conditional cash transfer scheme — not a drug entitlement (that's JSSK) or an insurance scheme. It gives cash incentives to BPL women who deliver in government facilities.
Well done. JSY is India's flagship conditional cash transfer for institutional delivery — the key supply-side enabler that raised institutional delivery from 39% (NFHS-3) to 89% (NFHS-5).
